prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts a studio corner with a curved white backdrop sweep against the back wall (~3–4 m away in frames 1–3), a recessed doorway to the back-left, and two tripod-mounted softbox lights framing the foreground on the left (~2–2.5 m) and right (~1.5–2 m). A man in a head-mounted camera strap stands in front of the backdrop (~2.5–3 m from the camera wearer) with a small round stool within his arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m to his left in frame 1), then reaches down to grab the stool in frame 2 and sits on it in frame 3 while facing toward the camera wearer with his head tilted downward. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer approaches the seated man until he is within ~1.2–1.5 m in frame 4 and within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m) in frame 5, where the softboxes pass out of the side of the view, the man's lower body drops below the bottom frame edge, and the camera wearer's own right arm enters from the bottom-right to touch the man's left shoulder while the man turns his head to his right (frame left) away from the wearer. The continuous luminance gradient makes the curved geometry of the floor-to-wall backdrop sweep and the rapid reduction in distance from ~3 m to ~0.5 m much clearer than in the featureless white RGB backdrop. However, the depth map is unreliable on the right softbox diffuser in frames 1–3 (which saturates to pure white as if closer than 0.5 m due to its bright illumination), loses the thin tripod legs and overhead backdrop rollers in the dark background, and flattens the relative depth between the backdrop and the dark doorway in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground man ('person', pink mask) standing ~2.5–3 m in front of the camera wearer and the small stool ('chair', purple mask) ~0.3–0.5 m to his left (frame right) in frame 1. In frames 2 and 3, as the man reaches for and sits on the stool (~2.5–3 m away, torso facing the camera wearer), his body and legs occlude the stool enough that only his single pink 'person' mask remains visible. As the camera wearer steps forward to ~1.2–1.5 m in frame 4 and within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m) in frame 5, the man's pink mask expands across the lower-left foreground with his legs cropped out of view below the bottom edge, while a second 'person' mask (brown) appears at the bottom-right in frame 5 for the camera wearer's extended right forearm and hand contacting the man's shoulder. This map clearly separates the boundary between the camera wearer's reaching arm and the seated man's shoulder in frame 5, and pinpoints the exact frame where the stool becomes heavily occluded by the man's legs, which is less immediate in RGB. However, it is unreliable for broader scene layout because it completely omits the studio softboxes, light stands, backdrop rolls, and background door, fails to detect the visible portion of the stool beneath the man in frames 2–4, and leaks the man's pink mask onto the camera wearer's wrist and hand in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints (yellow body joints and links, magenta hand joints) of the single man in front of the camera wearer as their separation shrinks from ~2.5–3 m in frames 1–3 to ~1.2–1.5 m in frame 4 and ~0.4–0.6 m in frame 5. In frame 1, his shoulders and hips face the camera wearer with both elbows raised and hands within reach of his own collar, then in frames 2 and 3 his torso bends forward and his left wrist reaches down to the stool beside him before he sits with his knees bent and facial keypoints angled downward rather than looking directly at the camera wearer. In frame 4, his upper-body skeleton looms larger in the foreground with the lower legs cut off below the bottom border and a magenta hand cluster detected on his left hand (frame right), and by frame 5 his head turns sharply toward the left edge of the frame while the camera wearer's reaching arm enters from the bottom-right. The skeleton makes the man's joint angles, shoulder orientation, and head-pitch trajectory—especially his downward gaze during sitting and subsequent leftward head turn—explicit even where his dark cardigan blends with his trousers in RGB. However, the map provides no information about the stool, lighting equipment, or room walls, misses the fine finger keypoints in frames 1–3, and breaks down severely in frame 5 under extreme close-up occlusion by collapsing the torso into a flat horizontal bar and placing a single magenta hand cluster near the man's left shoulder where the camera wearer's hand is actually located.
